newsitem.title: ITALY: Interest rates on agenda at Italy question time.
newsitem.headline: Interest rates on agenda at Italy question time.

text.p: The hot topic of Italian interest rates will be on the agenda for parliamentary questions in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on Wednesday, an official statement said.

It said the televised session, beginning at 1300 GMT, would also deal with the autonomy of the Bank of Italy. Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi, Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and Transport Minister Claudio Burlando are due to take part.
The session allows ministers to reply to written parliamentary questions. It was not immediately clear who had requested discussion of interest rates and the central bank.

Central bank governor Antonio Fazio has come under intense pressure from the government, industrialists and union leaders to lower Italy's discount rate from its current 6.75 percent in the face of fast-declining inflation.
Fazio has not cut the rate since January and analysts say they are not sure when to expect action from an independent bank that has wrong-footed the market before.
Preliminary data point to June inflation of 1.4-1.5 percent against 1.6 percent in May.
Other items on the agenda include the organisation of international summits and port labour.
